title: Inverse image of a lifting torsor
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $0\to G\to I\to Q\to0$ a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] on the small etale site. Let $s\in Q(X)$, and let $T$ be a $G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor] equipped with an equivariant isomorphism to the sheaf of lifts of $s$ as in [lem-sc-torsor-h1]. Let $s_Y$ be the section of $f^{-1}Q$ obtained by the adjunction unit and the terminal-object comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero]. Then the set inverse image [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] of $T$ is isomorphic to the torsor of lifts of $s_Y$ in the pulled-back short exact sequence. The isomorphism is equivariant on the pulled-back sections, for the abelian inverse-image unit and the set inverse-image unit.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, label lemma-torsors-h1, fibre-of-a-section construction; inverse-image fibre argument from lem-sc-etale-torsor-inverse-image-extension step 2

proof.text: Use the canonical fibre comparison of [lem-sc-etale-inverse-image-lifts-fibre], with its equation for the underlying inclusion into the middle abelian sheaf.

Choose the given equivariant torsor isomorphism e. Set the desired isomorphism to the set inverse image of e followed by the fibre comparison. Naturality of the set adjunction unit transports sections through e. Apply subtype extensionality to the equivariance goal. The fibre inclusion equation, additivity of the abelian unit, and naturality of that unit with respect to the kernel inclusion prove equality of the underlying middle-object sections.

proof_origin.note: Lean proof by fibre inclusion compatibility, unit naturality, subtype extensionality and additivity. Original unit route retained.
